This queue is not moving. Greg, finance side, out of Chicago. So what does your company do?
Andreia, nice to meet you. I work for a company that builds tax and finance software, and I am the person who looks after the partners outside Brazil.
Tax software. That is a crowded market. What do people come to you for?
Usually compliance. The pain point that brings them to us is almost never the price. It is the audit that nobody could answer last year.
That I understand. We have three providers and none of them talk to each other. How big are the companies you work with?
Groups with a headcount over two thousand, which is where payroll stops being straightforward. We rolled it out in four countries last year.
Four countries at once. How long from signature to the day it actually works?
About five months, and we never go live on a Friday. Come by the stand later and I will walk you through it. And you, what brings the finance side to a software conference?

Say that again for me, a little slower.

People ask me what I sell and I always want to say software, because that is the easy answer, but it is not really true. What I sell is the answer to a question somebody could not answer last year. I had a client, a group with about four thousand people, and their headcount had doubled in eighteen months, and they had opened in two more countries, and the old system kept working the whole time. That was the problem. It kept working. Nobody noticed that the numbers had stopped being right until an auditor asked for one report and the whole thing came apart. So the one thing I have learned to do, and it took me years, is to ask what went wrong last year before I show anybody anything. The pain point is never on the list they send you. It is the thing nobody wants to put in writing.

We looked at four providers and honestly the demos were all the same. The one we chose was not the cheapest and their demo was not even the best one. They were the only ones who asked us what had gone wrong the year before, and I remember thinking, well, at least these people are paying attention. Now, we made one mistake and it was ours, not theirs. We went live on a Friday, at the end of the month, which is the worst possible combination, and of course the first payroll run failed and there was nobody in the building. What saved that weekend was a person on their side who called me on Saturday morning and walked my team through it screen by screen, for two days, on the phone. I still have his number in my phone. I would move providers before I would give up that number.
